To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) MFCC is the optimal parametrization, (2) GMM-MMI is the optimal classifier, (3) 3-second data is sufficient for recognition, (4) none of the six classifier is superior to each of the others, (5) context recognition accuracy depends on the user, and (6) the accuracy depends on the phone used.
GMM-MMI is the best classifier in terms of overall accuracy, VQ is the best in terms of user accuracy, and GMM-SVM is the best in phone accuracy.
GMM-MMI classifier performs the best, VQ classifier performs second best, and SVM classifier is not the best classifier for the problem at hand.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of an efficient context recognition system from mobile audio data.
a thorough analysis of context recognition from short audio records in a mobile environment using different classifiers.

the following: (i) audio context classification using MFCC parametrization; (ii) extensive comparison of six classifiers, namely kNN, VQ, GMM-ML, GMM-MMi, GMM-SVM and SVM with GLDS; and (iii) analysis of the performance of each classifier in class-, user- and phone-specific scenarios.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the classifiers varies with respect to different contexts.
the best classifier is the classifier with the best parameter setting for the given application.
the choice of classifier depends on the context of application and the type of data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a given application, the choice of the classifier depends upon the application requirements, and the best performing classifier is not necessarily superior to the other classifiers.
the best performance of context recognition from 3-second audio segments using MFCC features is obtained by GMM-MMI, which is 2.6 percentage points better than the next best classifier, VQ.
, in the case of short audio data records (3 s), the context recognition problem can be solved with a high level of confidence by using a combination of MFCC features and VQ or GMM-MMI classifiers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of classifier should be guided by the application at hand.
, for a given classifier, the performance of the system is highly dependent on the choice of the feature representation and parameter optimization.

, for a given application, the choice of the classifier is more important than the feature extraction method, and, in particular, the choice of classifier should be guided by the application and the data.
